title: Boss: The Bookshop Reports
summary: Projections, paging, grouping and safe SQL, all answered by the database.

steps.title: Reports night
body: The bookshop owner wants three reports. The model is the one from this module (authors and books, five books). Every report must be computed **by the database**: the tests read the SQL your code ran.
class Author { int Id; string Name; string Country; List<Book> Books; }
class Book   { int Id; string Title; int Year; int Pages; string Genre; int AuthorId; Author Author; }

The tests fill it with five books: Earthsea (Le Guin, 1968, 183 pages, Fantasy), The Dispossessed (Le Guin, 1974, 387, SciFi), Dune (Herbert, 1965, 412, SciFi), Emma (Austen, 1815, 474, Classic) and Persuasion (Austen, 1817, 249, Classic). Le Guin and Herbert are from the US, Austen from the UK.

steps.title: The shelf list
prompt: `List<ShelfRow> Shelf(LibraryDb db, int page, int pageSize)`: every book as `record ShelfRow(string Title, string Author, string Era)`, ordered by author name then title, paged (1-based).
`Era` is `"Classic"` before 1900, otherwise `"Modern"`, computed **in SQL** (a C# conditional `b.Year < 1900 ? "Classic" : "Modern"` inside the `Select` translates to `CASE WHEN`).
starter: List<ShelfRow> Shelf(LibraryDb db, int page, int pageSize) => [];
record ShelfRow(string Title, string Author, string Era);
solution: List<ShelfRow> Shelf(LibraryDb db, int page, int pageSize) =>
record ShelfRow(string Title, string Author, string Era);

var herbert = new Author { Name = "Herbert", Country = "US" };
var austen = new Author { Name = "Austen", Country = "UK" };
new Book { Title = "Earthsea", Year = 1968, Pages = 183, Genre = "Fantasy", Author = leGuin },
new Book { Title = "The Dispossessed", Year = 1974, Pages = 387, Genre = "SciFi", Author = leGuin },
new Book { Title = "Dune", Year = 1965, Pages = 412, Genre = "SciFi", Author = herbert },
new Book { Title = "Emma", Year = 1815, Pages = 474, Genre = "Classic", Author = austen },

steps.title: Genre statistics
prompt: Add `List<GenreStats> Stats(LibraryDb db)` returning one `record GenreStats(string Genre, int Books, int Pages, double AveragePages)` per genre, ordered by `Pages` descending.
Keep your `Shelf` and `ShelfRow` from the last step.
starter: List<ShelfRow> Shelf(LibraryDb db, int page, int pageSize) =>

record GenreStats(string Genre, int Books, int Pages, double AveragePages);
solution: .Select(g => new GenreStats(g.Key, g.Count(), g.Sum(b => b.Pages), g.Average(b => b.Pages)))

hints: `GroupBy(b => b.Genre).Select(g => new GenreStats(g.Key, g.Count(), g.Sum(b => b.Pages), g.Average(b => b.Pages)))`
EF Core cannot sort by a property of a record it builds: sort the groups first, `OrderByDescending(g => g.Sum(b => b.Pages))`, then `Select`.

steps.title: The author lookup
prompt: Add `List<string> AuthorsLike(LibraryDb db, string pattern)`: names of authors whose name matches a SQL `LIKE` pattern given by the user (for example `"%er%"`), with how many books each has, like `"Herbert (1)"`, ordered by name.

Use **`FromSql`** for the pattern match (`SELECT * FROM Authors WHERE Name LIKE {pattern}`), then compose LINQ on top for the count and the order. The pattern comes from a user, so it must be a parameter.

Dojo.Eq("names with 'e'", new List<string> { "Austen (2)", "Herbert (1)", "Le Guin (2)" }, AuthorsLike(dojoDb, "%e%"));
Dojo.Eq("an injection attempt finds nothing", new List<string>(), AuthorsLike(dojoDb, "x' OR '1'='1"));
